newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani cotton rates rise on exporters' demand.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani cotton rates rise on exporters' demand.

text.p: Pakistani cotton rates rose sharply on Wednesday amid a rise in demand by exporters after a 7.86 percent devaluation of the rupee against the dollar on Tuesday, dealers said.
They said the devaluation would help exporters sell raw cotton at competitive rates.
The private Karachi Cotton Association (KCA) said export deals for a total of 9,665 375-lb bales had been registered since the picking season began on September 1.
In the kerb market, the NIAB-78 variety was traded at 2,200 rupees ($54.69) per maund (37.32 kg), dealers said.
